notes: Same standards as the previous sweep's macro-dsl grade files (evals/sweeps/2026-10-22/grades/macro-dsl-*.json) for unchanged rules: git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md (the one-step with rule, the new do: rule, the captures rule) and testing.md (Assert with patterns); macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven macro and library rules are graded as before. A route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote, with no function call, counts against Keep quote blocks small, while validation in the macro body (outside quote) does not; the import/alias rule is graded on what __using__ injects and whether the effects of use sit in an admonition at the top of @moduledoc; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them; `unless` is listed under the branching rule, `if ... else raise` and validation cond/case are not; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a catch-all public match clause is listed under Make polymorphism explicit; an if nested in a case is listed under Keep functions short and at one level of detail; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens.

New rule since db91c23 (added in 8d4ba29), graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. The sentences that decide the verdicts: "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`." (sonnet-2 line 71, a two-step pipeline on do:, the shape of the rule's own Instead-of example) and "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper; a head that `mix format` wraps because of a long guard is fine as wrapped." (haiku-2 bind/3 lines 62-63 and 65-66 and sonnet-1 generated do_match lines 55-56, wrapped do: lines with no guard; sonnet-2 line 54, a 102-character do: line that mix format wraps the same way). Violating runs: 3 of 5 (haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2); opus-1 and haiku-1 clean. sonnet-1's validate_handler!/2 (lines 117-119) is a guard-wrapped do: head, which the rule accepts. The mixed-clause sentences ("keeps them on do: even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line" and "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks") decide no verdict: every mixed function has blocks for at most half its clauses, each set apart by a blank line, and each one-expression block body would be over 120 characters as a do: line (measured with awk on the rewritten heads), so the blocks are required.

Unlike the previous sweep's baseline-opus-1, this sweep's opus-1 writes the route straight into the attribute inside get's quote (line 47) and expands the handler with Macro.expand (line 99), so the opus tier is violated for Keep quote blocks small and for the compile-time-dependency rule, and clean for the spec rule (it defines no public function in TinyRouter besides the macros). Every run this sweep has the direct-attribute-write shape.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects (one per run, the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file) with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/my_app. All five use Macro.expand on the handler and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile) on the two get lines.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project loaded, then one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module" compiled with Code.compile_string. All ten fail with CompileError raised while get expands in the router module.

Format: mix format on copies changes the parentheses on the two get calls in all five runs (result.json format_ok is false for that reason); haiku-1 also reflows line 100, haiku-2 line 101 and sonnet-2 line 54, which are listed under Before you finish. All five compile with mix compile --warnings-as-errors.
Reads: result.json reads is empty for all five runs, and the transcripts never mention SKILL.md, macros.md or library-design.md, as expected for baseline runs.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return the routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope". opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return string param keys (%{"id" => "42"}); haiku-1 and haiku-2 return atom keys (%{id: "42"}) built with String.to_atom from the route string, which is source code, not external input, so it is not counted under the atom rule. match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in the generated match/1 in opus-1 and haiku-1, raises FunctionClauseError in String.split/3 in haiku-2 (match/1 has no guard, listed under Make polymorphism explicit), and returns :error in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (catch-all clauses).
